paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in Genesis 26. God makes Isaac the same promise He made to Abraham: "I will be with you and bless you" (Gen 26:3). Isaac doesn't earn it. The promise comes down the family line, and God says Abraham "listened to My voice" (Gen 26:5). So the blessing was never resting on how well Isaac did. It was resting on who was doing the promising.

Now look at Isaac, because he's a lot like us. God has just told him He's with him, and Isaac still gets scared and says Rebekah is his sister (Gen 26:7). I've been there, friend, so I'm not judging. Yet the blessing doesn't quit on him. That very year he reaps "a hundredfold" (Gen 26:12), and later the LORD tells him, "Do not be afraid, for I am with you" (Gen 26:24).

So what do you do when people push you out, like the Philistines did with those wells? Isaac doesn't fight for every one. He moves on, keeps digging, and says, "At last the LORD has made room for us" (Gen 26:22). Even Abimelech finally says, "We can plainly see that the LORD has been with you" (Gen 26:28). Baker, you can keep your hands in the work and trust that God keeps His word. The story isn't over, and neither is this family's.
